text.p: First Engineering Ltd said on Monday it expected market conditions and profits to improve throughout the remainder of the year after reporting net earnings for the year to March 31 down 44.9 percent.
"The directors expect market conditions in the electronics industry for the current year to improve," First Engineering said in a statement.
The firm said while competitive forces would remain strong, increases in operating costs were expected to be moderate.
Consequently, "barring any unforeseen circumstances, group performance for the current year is expected to improve", the statement added.
Earlier electronics assembler and injection moulding firm First Engineering reported net earnings of Singapore $1.2 million, down from S$2.2 million previously.
Earnings fell despite a year on year jump of 51 percent in revenues, which rose to S$73.5 million from S$48.7 million.

The company said earnings from its electronics assembly business were eroded by intense competition in the electronics market place and the costs of moving its production activities to Malaysia from Singapore.
Production costs, however. were expected to deliver savings because of the generally lower cost environment, the company said.
